complexityAnalysis.taskTitle: The workspace lives on the server, and the browser holds a cache of it.
complexityAnalysis.expansionPrompt: (1) server schema and read path; (2) local repository adapter; (3) optimistic write path with revision and refusal; (4) offline queue; (5) live multi-client propagation; (6) first-sign-in import; (7) server schema migrations.
complexityAnalysis.reasoning: Largest architectural task: server authority, one persistence boundary, optimistic/offline writes, live sync, import and migrations, with multi-device consistency risk.

complexityAnalysis.taskTitle: A backup exists, and someone has restored from it.
complexityAnalysis.reasoning: Mostly provider configuration, retention, export and a restore drill; low technical novelty but operational discipline required.

complexityAnalysis.taskTitle: One person holds a card's pen at a time.
complexityAnalysis.expansionPrompt: (1) lock table and conditional endpoints; (2) presence channel and client lock state; (3) lease acquisition, heartbeat, release and expiry; (4) read-only drawer, card mark, bulk refusal and arrangement exclusion tests.
complexityAnalysis.reasoning: Distributed lease requires server arbitration, live presence, heartbeat/expiry, read-only UI states and race-prone two-client behavior.

complexityAnalysis.taskTitle: A refused write keeps the words and says what happened.
complexityAnalysis.reasoning: Contained UX error handling for two refusal states; must preserve local text, explain refusal, and prevent retry loops.

complexityAnalysis.taskTitle: A workspace has members, and a member's role decides what they may do.
complexityAnalysis.expansionPrompt: (1) workspace entity and scoping every persisted entity; (2) membership and invitation acceptance; (3) role table, API enforcement, removal and last-owner guard.
complexityAnalysis.reasoning: Schema-wide workspace scoping plus roles, invitations, removal and escalation guards; changes are cross-cutting.

complexityAnalysis.taskTitle: A board can be shared as a read-only link, and the link can be revoked.
complexityAnalysis.reasoning: Bound token, read-only board rendering, API write guard, revocation and optional expiry; clear and contained.

complexityAnalysis.taskTitle: The app is usable with a keyboard and a screen reader.
complexityAnalysis.expansionPrompt: (1) focus trap, Escape return, live announcements and reduced motion; (2) keyboard alternatives for drag actions, accessible names and axe CI.
complexityAnalysis.reasoning: Accessibility pass spans modal focus, announcements, and keyboard parity for drag interactions across the board.

complexityAnalysis.taskTitle: The product says what it does with your data, and can delete it.
complexityAnalysis.reasoning: Public policy pages, export, verified deletion and support/changelog; process-driven with straightforward data removal.

complexityAnalysis.taskTitle: The project runs on a machine its owner controls.
complexityAnalysis.expansionPrompt: (1) Dockerfile and Node entry; (2) compose file and volumes; (3) first-run migrations and owner bootstrap; (4) health endpoint and self-hoster documentation.
complexityAnalysis.reasoning: Packaging work more than product invention; dependable first run, persistence on volumes and honest docs drive the complexity.

complexityAnalysis.taskTitle: One permission model decides who may do what.
complexityAnalysis.reasoning: Pure, isolated domain module with a single role/action matrix and exhaustive tests; no integration surfaces.

complexityAnalysis.taskTitle: The schema separates instance access from workspace authority.
complexityAnalysis.expansionPrompt: (1) migration 0003 and data mapping from existing members; (2) account, session, invitation and audit tables; (3) first-run administrator bootstrap and dual-runtime migration tests.
complexityAnalysis.reasoning: High-risk data migration that splits an overloaded table, reissues invitations as hashed tokens, preserves existing authority, and must run unchanged on D1 and file SQLite.

complexityAnalysis.taskTitle: Every API write checks the role, and reads it live.
complexityAnalysis.expansionPrompt: (1) live instance/workspace role resolution and middleware guards; (2) status semantics and session payload hardening; (3) role-change, removal and forged-authority tests.
complexityAnalysis.reasoning: Cross-cutting API authorization with live role reads, no client trust, correct status codes, and immediate role-change effect.

complexityAnalysis.taskTitle: A new instance is closed by default, and the first person is its administrator.
complexityAnalysis.expansionPrompt: (1) instance access setting and identify() refusal rules; (2) admin setting surface, dev-switch warning and no-leak tests.
complexityAnalysis.reasoning: Identity admission policy with first-user bootstrap, invitation precedence and enumeration-resistant refusals.

complexityAnalysis.taskTitle: Active and inactive mean one thing everywhere.
complexityAnalysis.expansionPrompt: (1) deactivate/reactivate transaction, session revocation and last-admin self-protection guards; (2) directory/picker treatment, invitation behavior and audit tests.
complexityAnalysis.reasoning: Status semantics must be consistent across sign-in, sessions, pickers, assignments and admin guards, with preservation of history.

complexityAnalysis.taskTitle: An invitation is a single-use link, not an email row.
complexityAnalysis.expansionPrompt: (1) token hashing, create/list/resend/revoke endpoints; (2) public inspection, accept-after-sign-in and enumeration/replay tests.
complexityAnalysis.reasoning: Security-sensitive single-use invitations with hashed tokens, expiry, revocation and anti-enumeration behavior.

complexityAnalysis.taskTitle: A profile the person owns.
complexityAnalysis.reasoning: Profile CRUD with read-only email, identity unlinking, avatar limits and soft-failing UI; standard validation work.

complexityAnalysis.taskTitle: Sessions are visible, revocable, and expire honestly.
complexityAnalysis.expansionPrompt: (1) session metadata, lifetime and throttled last-seen updates; (2) user/admin revocation and cookie hardening tests.
complexityAnalysis.reasoning: Session lifecycle security with per-session expiry, cookie flags, multi-session revocation and admin override.

complexityAnalysis.taskTitle: Every change to access is in the audit log.
complexityAnalysis.expansionPrompt: (1) single record() helper, event vocabulary and payload rules; (2) transactional wiring across access mutations and retention tests.
complexityAnalysis.reasoning: Append-only audit across many mutations; key complexity is transactional consistency, safe payloads and retention.

complexityAnalysis.taskTitle: The People screen.
complexityAnalysis.expansionPrompt: (1) admin list with search, filters, sort and server-side pagination; (2) person drawer actions, guardrails and feedback; (3) empty/error states, accessibility and Playwright coverage.
complexityAnalysis.reasoning: Admin screen with many actions, self/last-admin guardrails, accessible drawer/table, and server-backed pagination.

complexityAnalysis.taskTitle: The Invitations screen.
complexityAnalysis.expansionPrompt: (1) invitation list and create/copy-once dialog; (2) resend/revoke and accept-through-sign-in test.
complexityAnalysis.reasoning: Focused admin UI over existing invitation API; complexity is copy-once secrecy and state coverage.

complexityAnalysis.taskTitle: Workspace members and their roles.
complexityAnalysis.expansionPrompt: (1) workspace member list, role change, removal and last-admin guard; (2) workspace invitation flow and shared role/guard components with People screen.
complexityAnalysis.reasoning: Workspace admin surface that reuses role/guard patterns; key concerns are workspace-level scope, invitation distinction and last-admin rule.

complexityAnalysis.taskTitle: Admin -> Audit and Health.
complexityAnalysis.expansionPrompt: (1) audit list, filters and sentence rendering with authority scoping; (2) health/error inbox, posture banners and count consistency tests.
complexityAnalysis.reasoning: Read-only admin screens over existing tables; mostly filtering, pagination, scoped visibility and honest status display.

complexityAnalysis.taskTitle: Delete and erase are different promises.
complexityAnalysis.expansionPrompt: (1) delete/erase mechanics and history preservation; (2) confirmations, audit safety and re-invitation tests.
complexityAnalysis.reasoning: Two erasure semantics that must preserve history and referential anchors while respecting self/last-admin guards and audit privacy.

complexityAnalysis.taskTitle: The conveniences: allowed domains, bulk actions and CSV.
complexityAnalysis.expansionPrompt: (1) allowed-domain access rule and Admin UI; (2) all-or-nothing bulk actions and RFC 4180 CSV export with server-side scale.
complexityAnalysis.reasoning: Access policy convenience plus bulk operations with all-or-nothing judgement and safe CSV export.

complexityAnalysis.taskTitle: Groups: a role granted once to many.
complexityAnalysis.expansionPrompt: (1) groups, membership and workspace role assignment model; (2) effective role union, last-admin interaction and audit tests.
complexityAnalysis.reasoning: Group-based role union changes permission evaluation and last-admin behavior; deferred but nontrivial.

complexityAnalysis.taskTitle: A custom role label that grants nothing.
complexityAnalysis.reasoning: Cosmetic label only; main challenge is enforcing no permission path and deleting labels without impacting roles.

complexityAnalysis.taskTitle: API tokens with scopes.
complexityAnalysis.expansionPrompt: (1) token minting, hashing, scope and expiry logic; (2) revocation, admin visibility and scope/role enforcement tests.
complexityAnalysis.reasoning: Token lifecycle security with scopes, owner-role caps, secret handling and admin audit.

complexityAnalysis.taskTitle: A second factor, if a deployment ever needs one.
complexityAnalysis.reasoning: Deferred WebAuthn second-factor policy; current work is trigger/recording and a safe rollout shape, not implementation.
